hints: Focus on which functional groups react with sodium, remember both alcohol -OH and carboxylic acid -CO2H give H2 with Na.
Count the total number of -OH groups (alcohol plus acid) in each of the four structures to test statement 1.
Classify each alcohol as primary, secondary or tertiary by looking at the carbon attached to the OH, then check statements 2 and 3.
walkthrough:
**Recall reaction with sodium**

Sodium reacts with any O-H that is acidic enough, that is alcohols and carboxylic acids. Each $\text{-OH}$ group provides one H, and 2 moles of $\text{-OH}$ react with 2 moles of Na to give $\text{H}_2$.

$$2\text{R-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Test statement 1 by counting OH groups**

$\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$ has 2 alcohol OH. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$ has 2 alcohol OH. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ has 1 alcohol OH + 1 acid OH. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ has 1 alcohol OH + 1 acid OH.

So each isomer has 2 reactive H in total, one mole reacts with two moles of Na. Statement 1 is correct.

**Classify primary, secondary, tertiary alcohols**

A primary alcohol is $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-OH}$, secondary is $\text{R}_2\text{CH-OH}$, tertiary is $\text{R}_3\text{C-OH}$.

Isomer 1: two $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, both primary. Isomer 2: one $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ primary + one $\text{-CH(OH)-}$ secondary. Isomer 3: one $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ primary. Isomer 4: one $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ secondary only.

**Conclude on statements 2 and 3**

None of the four contains a tertiary $\text{R}_3\text{C-OH}$ group, so statement 2 which claims only one does is incorrect. Isomer 4 has no primary alcohol, only a secondary alcohol, so statement 3 which claims they all do is incorrect.

Only statement 1 is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is correct but statements 2 and 3 are false because no isomer has a tertiary alcohol and isomer 4 has no primary alcohol.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is false. All alcohol groups here are primary or secondary, none is tertiary.
options.C: Incorrect. This option claims 2 and 3 are correct. Both are false. A common trap is to misclassify $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ in isomer 4 as primary or tertiary instead of secondary.
options.D: Correct. This option states only 1 is correct. Each isomer has exactly two O-H groups that react with Na, no isomer has a tertiary alcohol, and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ lacks a primary alcohol.
